title: A Harbor for the Atlas
premise: In 1917, in a fog-bound port city, battlefield nurse Tamsin Sandoval keeps a secret ledger of soldiers' names that official reports have erased—men written off as deserters, dead, or never existed. When a census taker named Elias Wren asks one question too many about the unregistered wounded sheltered in the old sailmaker's workshop where she works, Tamsin realizes her invisibility is a fiction the war can no longer afford. As military investigators close in and the river ice begins to groan toward spring breakup, Tamsin and Elias must finish transcribing and delivering the ledger to a naval inquiry before the workshop—and everyone hidden inside it—is seized. The book ends with the ice breaking: the ledger reaches the inquiry at terrible cost, Elias takes the fall for the harbor's sins, and Tamsin, no longer invisible, chooses to stand publicly as witness rather than flee.
about_author: Jude Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime hospital records before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the tide charts still hang in the post office, and they remain stubbornly interested in the names history tried to lose.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Opening in the sailmaker's workshop, Tamsin tends an unregistered soldier and adds his name to her hidden ledger, establishing her quiet system of record-keeping. Emotional beat: weary resolve—the reader understands she has chosen this burden deliberately and knows its danger.

chapters.title: A Question of Residence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Census taker Elias Wren arrives to count the harbor district and lingers over the workshop's impossible numbers—one bed, six coats, too many boots. Tamsin deflects him, but he leaves unconvinced. Emotional beat: first crack in her armor; fear sharpening into vigilance.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias files his census forms but cannot stop thinking about the discrepancy; flashbacks reveal he lost a brother whose name vanished from an official casualty list. Emotional beat: private grief curdling into suspicion—he begins pulling harbor records after hours.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A wounded officer, Captain Merrick, convalesces in the workshop and nearly discovers the ledger; Tamsin lies to him fluently and hates herself for it. Emotional beat: guilt—she realizes protecting the names has made her a keeper of deceptions that cut both ways.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias returns under pretext of correcting the count and finds Tamsin boiling bandages for men who officially do not exist. Instead of reporting her, he asks to see the ledger. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance—two people recognizing each other across a line neither meant to cross.

chapters.title: Six Names from the Marne
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She shows Elias three pages only; among them he finds a name connected to his brother's unit. He agrees to help but insists the ledger must go somewhere it can't be burned. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an intruder—Tamsin hasn't dared plan an ending before.

chapters.title: The Naval Inquiry
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias learns a naval board will convene when the ice breaks, giving them a deadline: deliver the ledger before the river opens and the workshop loses its cover of chaos. Emotional beat: urgency crystallizing into purpose—the clock starts here.

chapters.title: Merrick's Memory
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Captain Merrick, recovering, begins recalling what happened to the men Tamsin has listed—orders he signed. His loyalty to the army wars with his conscience. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness entangled; Tamsin must decide whether he is a threat or an ally.

chapters.title: A Harbor Full of Ears
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A military investigator, Sergeant Quill, arrives tracing a deserter's trail to the waterfront. Elias feeds him false directions while Tamsin moves two patients by fishing boat through the fog. Emotional beat: breathless complicity—the alliance becomes action, and there is no walking back.

chapters.title: The Cost of Ink
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Copying the ledger for safekeeping, Tamsin reads every entry aloud to herself and finally grieves the men she couldn't save. Elias stays up with her. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared mourning—the love story surfaces quietly, without either naming it.

chapters.title: Quill Closes In
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Quill matches Elias's census corrections to the workshop and confronts him privately, offering immunity in exchange for testimony against Tamsin. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth turned inward—Elias must choose which version of himself survives.

chapters.title: The Workshop Stands
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Quill raids the harbor district but finds the workshop legally clean; Merrick, unprompted, covers for them with a fabricated duty roster. Emotional beat: vertiginous relief and shame—Tamsin owes her safety to the very officer class her ledger indicts.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias tells Tamsin about Quill's offer, hiding nothing. She is furious, then honest: if the ledger dies with her, the names die twice. They agree to split the copy—his insurance, hers. Emotional beat: trust forged in full disclosure; love admitted in practical terms.

chapters.title: What Merrick Knows
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Merrick confesses the orders behind the omitted names and offers to testify, knowing it ends his career and likely his freedom. Emotional beat: moral reversal—the man who wrote men out of existence now demands to be written back in, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: The Ice Groans
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The river ice begins cracking early; the inquiry date moves up, and Quill requests warrants for the workshop. Elias races to secure a hearing slot through a sympathetic clerk. Emotional beat: time collapsing—every errand now carries the weight of everything.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Fog
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. One of the hidden soldiers, terrified, trades information to Quill for passage home. The raid comes at dawn; Tamsin burns nothing but hides the original ledger in the one place no one searches—a coffin bound for the naval cemetery. Emotional beat: heartbreak and cold clarity; sentiment is a luxury the work cannot afford.

chapters.title: Arrest at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Quill arrests Tamsin for harboring deserters; Elias surrenders the copied ledger to the inquiry clerk as evidence, forcing the board to acknowledge it exists. Emotional beat: sacrifice made strategic—Elias gives up his anonymity and his safety net in a single act.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Before the naval inquiry, Merrick testifies, the coffin-ledger is produced, and the omitted names are read aloud into the record while Quill argues sedition. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken plainly in a room built for euphemism, with the ice audibly breaking outside.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The inquiry validates the ledger but needs someone to blame; Elias claims sole authorship of the copies to shield Tamsin. She refuses to let him, standing as witness in her own name. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—both choose truth over protection, together.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Elias receives a reduced sentence for records tampering; Merrick accepts court-martial; the workshop's patients are quietly pardoned as 'administrative errors.' Tamsin walks the frozen shore reading the ledger one last time. Emotional beat: bitter, hard-won justice—outside the law, then absorbed by it, imperfectly.

chapters.title: The River Opens
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Spring breakup; the ice goes out with a sound like artillery. Tamsin visits Elias before his transport leaves and gives him the original ledger's first page—his brother's name, restored. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into promise; love stated at last, in the language they share.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Atlas
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, epilogue. Months later, Tamsin keeps the workshop running as an unofficial records office for families searching for lost men, the atlas of names growing thicker. A letter arrives from Elias, due home by autumn. Emotional beat: resolution without erasure—the harbor holds, the work continues, and visibility, once feared, has become her vocation.
